blogs.title: Past Action Persists -- How Farahi Clarifies Pending Enforcement Proceedings Under Foia’s §552(b)(7)(A)
description: (1) Judge Katsas confirms that an investigation deemed ongoing can survive a decade‑long lapse without losing its qualifying status.
(2) The decision hinges upon FBI affidavits stating investigators were still gathering facts meant for prosecution—a scenario common in counter‑terrorism files.
(3) This expands prior doctrine concerning what counts as ‘pending’ under Section seven(a), redefining prosecutors’ temporal latitude.

blogs.title: "Deference Amid Secrecy" -- How Courts Treat Agency Determinations About Ultimate Law Enforcement Purpose
description: (1) Katsas cites Campbell and CNSS showing bright judicial deference whenever an agency claims activity falls squarely under its core duties.
(2) National‑security concerns magnify that pushback against probing factual bases furnished via sealed affidavits.
(3) The ruling thereby reaffirms judges’ restraint toward conclusive executive statements even when evidence remains unstated.

blogs.title: "When Nothing Seeks Release" -- Segregation Challenges Within Massified Confidential Files
description: (1) Judge Katsas held that hundreds of pages jammed together cannot be trimmed out simply because isolated segments seem harmless.
(2) Intermixed annotations, metadata markings, or subtle indication shifts made it impossible to separate exempt material meaningfully.
(3) He clarified authorities cannot publish parts unless whole records lend themselves neatly away from secrecy burdens.
